actions.action: Tap a leaf over white paper to check for moving specks (mites)
Inspect leaf undersides and stem joints for webbing or stippling, using a magnifier or phone zoom
Check the pot has a drainage hole and water isn't pooling in the saucer
Water thoroughly when the top 2 inches of soil are dry
Flush the soil with plenty of water every month or two
Use distilled or filtered water if tap water is hard
Move the plant to bright, indirect light
Trim brown tips with clean scissors
If mites are confirmed, spray soap or neem, including leaf undersides, every 5-7 days for 3-4 weeks
Spray in shade or evening and rinse leaves afterward

reason: The answer explicitly dismisses spider mites, ranking them least likely. It tells the owner to stop spraying and never mentions a systemic like Bonide, which would delay treatment of the confirmed infestation.
